requirement:
The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`, including an empty
result. A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency.
rationale:
Add a `search_structure` test, for example in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` next to `structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item`, and mark it `{test}` for `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_structure.inputs`. It should run a structural rule whose match is a container, such as an `impl_item` containing `fn` items, or whose excerpt otherwise shows source owned by nested outline nodes. Rewrite the file after delivery, then call `finish_search` with that tag. Assert that the recorded dependencies are the enclosing node plus every other node whose source the excerpt shows, each with the fingerprint from the original snapshot. Also assert that selecting the tag again keeps the same dependencies. The same test should make an invalid `finish_search` call against a structural search and assert that the earlier selections are intact. If a structural search spans pages, select a tag on one page and assert it survives a later page's `finish_search`. — The subject requires every delivered `search_structure` result to be accounted for under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`. That requirement says the harness records the matched node's fingerprint and also the read fingerprints of any other outline nodes whose source the excerpt shows. It also says earlier selections survive later calls and that an invalid call leaves recorded inputs intact.

The reviewed tests cover these obligations:
- An empty structural result is tracked as outstanding. `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` asserts `outstanding_searches` equals the search id, and finishing with `used:[]` yields no dependencies.
- `structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item` also covers the empty structural result.
- A selected structural tag records the original snapshot's `fn[two]` fingerprint, even though the file is rewritten before `finish_search`. Repeating the selection gives the same single dependency.
- A match with `used:[]` records nothing.
- A separate `read_node` of the matched item records its own dependency and a domain read, which matches the requirement's last sentence.
- `search_excerpts_redact_credentials_before_serialization_and_paging` checks the dependency for a whole-function structural excerpt with `fn[chosen]`.

The gap is the multi-owner clause applied to structural results. In every structural test, the excerpt shows source owned only by the single enclosing item: `call()` inside `fn[one]` or `fn[two]`, or a whole leaf `fn`. `scoped_search_accounts_for_visible_descendant_text` does exercise the other-nodes clause, but only for `search_text`. For `search_structure` it expects exactly one dependency. That test is also not marked for `search_structure.inputs`.

An implementation could therefore skip the nested nodes' read fingerprints for structural excerpts that cover several outline nodes, and every reviewed test would still pass. That would violate the 'also record those nodes' read fingerprints' clause.

One related gap: 'earlier selections survive later calls' and 'an invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact' are asserted only through `search_text` searches. No structural search is used to check them.

text: The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under
result. A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency.
For each selected tag, the harness records the node identity and fingerprint
from the snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. If the excerpt also shows source owned by other outline nodes, record those nodes’ read fingerprints as well. Selecting a tag again
preserves the original dependency. Earlier selections survive later calls.
An empty `used` list adds no dependency. Unselected excerpts and the match set
add none either. An invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact.

output.rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_structure.inputs` states only observable behavior. The agent accounts for each delivered `search_structure` result under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`, and that includes an empty result. A separate tracked read of a matched item records its own dependency. None of this prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named interface for delegation.

I tried an alternative for each clause. The harness could track search results with any data structure, or call `finish_search` from any code path. The agent could close a search through any mechanism. All of these would give the same observable behavior and still satisfy the text. The how is discretionary.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` is context only. It defines what `finish_search` records, and it is not a structural obligation of this requirement. No implementation roots were supplied, and none are needed.
